Testimony ofRepresentative Anne-Marie Mastraccio presenting
LD 806, An Act to Amend the Scope of Practice for Expanded
Function Dental Assistants
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services
Senator Bailey, Representative Gramlich and fellow members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services. I am Anne-Marie Mastraccio, and I
represent House District 142, which includes part of the City of Sanford and the Village of
Springvale. I am here today to introduce LD 806, An Act to Amend the Scope of Practice for
Expanded Function Dental Assistants.

In Maine, an expanded function dental assistant (EFDA) is a certified dental assistant or a dental hygienist who has additional training and is then licensed by the Board of Dental Practice to perform a wider range of dental procedures. By virtue of the prerequisites for
certification/licensure as a dental hygienist or a nationally certified dental assistant, these" individuals are already allowed to take dental radiographs.
However, under the current Dental Practice Act, an EFDA is not authorized to take dental radiographs without first obtaining a second license from the board as a dental radiographer. LD
806 is designed to remove the necessity of paying an additional fee to the board of licensure for
the dental radiography authority. It does not change the scope of practice for an EFDA; it just
recognizes their already allowed scope and reduces the cost for licensure.
Thank you for your consideration, and I am happy to answer any questions you may have.

Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services, I am Annick Metoule, Oral Health Program Manager at Maine Primary Care Association (MPCA).
MPCA is a membership organization that includes Maine's Community Health Centers (CHCs), also known as Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs). Maine's FQHCs make up the largest independent primary care network in the state, providing high quality, affordable, and accessible primary and preventive medical, behavioral, and dental health services for over 200,000 people (1 in 6 Mainers) at more than 80 service delivery sites in all 16 Maine counties.
MPCA supports LD 806, which seeks to amend the scope of practice for Expanded Function Dental Assistants (EFDAs). Maine's FQHCs are acutely aware of the healthcare challenges faced by many Mainers, particularly those who are low-income and rely on MaineCare.
As we know, Maine is experiencing workforce shortages in many heath care professions, and dental providers are no exception. Access to dental care in Maine has become increasingly difficult, with many patients facing long wait lists and traveling significant distances to see a provider. With the recent expansion of MaineCare dental coverage for adult patients, the demand for services has grown. Unfortunately, the existing dental workforce is not sufficient to meet this rising need, leaving many without timely access to essential dental care, sometimes resulting in more serious health issues.
While we recognize that expanding the scope of practice for EFDAs is not an end solution for the dentist shortage, it offers a crucial piece of the puzzle. EFDAs play a vital role streamlining the delivery of care by reducing wait times and improving overall access to dental services. By empowering EFDAs to take on additional responsibilities, increased efficiency continues, and dentists can focus on more complex procedures. This collaborative approach is essential as we strive to meet the dental needs of our communities.
On behalf of Maine's Community Health Centers, thank you for considering my comments. Please do not hesitate to contact me with any follow up questions.

Dear Senator Bailey, Representative Gramlich and members of the Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial
Services Committee:

Thank you for allowing me to testify today in support of LD 806 An Act to Amend the Scope of Practice for Expanded Function Dental Assistants. I am Danica Loring, Director of Operations for Penobscot Community

Health Care, Dental Center.

,

V 6

PCHC is a non-profit, Federally Qualified Health Center that was founded in 1997. PCHC's Dental Center has
over 43 dental operatories and offers a wide range of services which include basic dental restorations, extractions, endodontic procedures, routine hygiene maintenance, orthodontics, and walk in care services to the
general public. Within the last 12 months alone, PCHC Dental Center has provided dental care to over 4,633
individuals which accounted for 18,552 encounters. Part of our dental team currently consists of 12 dental assistants, 3 of which are Expanded Functions Dental Assistants and an additional dental assistant which is
enrolled in the upcoming UMA EFDA course scheduled for this fall.

I am testifying today both in my capacity as a licensed Expanded Functions Dental Assistant in the state of Maine and as a dental leader responsible for the oversight of EFDAs at PCHC. To hold an Expanded Functions
Dental Assistant license, one is required to hold a Certified Dental Assistant Certificate from a board approved program or an active dental hygiene license in good standing issued under the laws of this state or another jurisdiction. Both avenues require successful completion of a radiology course or exam, which meets the Maine Dental Board's requirements for a Dental Radiographer License.
In Maine, the scope of practice for an EFDA does not include exposing and processing radiographs and because of this, it requires an EFDA to hold a dental radiography license and an EFDA license. Both licenses are to be
renewed every two years at $200 per license, in addition to their National Certified Dental Assisting.Certificate annual renewal of $75 equaling $275 every year for a total of $550 every two years, in comparison to the dental hygiene 2-year license renewal is $140 and dentist license renewal at $750. To further compare, the average
Maine salary for a general dentist is $192,269, a dental hygienist is $82,347, while an EFDA's average yearly salary is $46,081, almost half of a hygienist. What I have experienced and observed in my role is that many dental assistants are resistant to continuing their education to pursue an EFDA license due to financial
constraints, which licensing contributes to. With limited dental access and dental staffing shortages, we want to
encourage and support the EFDA scope of practice allowing additional access for patient care,` rather than
creating barriers for these individuals.

Testimony of the Maine Dental Association before the Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Committee
LD 806 An Act to Amend the Scope of Practice for Expanded Function Dental Assistants
In Support Public Hearing: Thursday, March 13, 2025
Senator Bailey, Representative Mathieson and Distinguished Members of the Health Coverage, Insurance and Financial Services Committee:
My name is Therese Cahill, and I serve as Executive Director of the Maine Dental Association. The MDA is a statewide association dedicated to advancing excellence in dentistry. Unfortunately, I am unable to attend today's Public Hearing.
The MDA represents 75% of the dentists in Maine; there are approximately 700 practicing and retired dentists who are active members of the association.
On behalf of the Maine Dental Association, I am respectfully providing testimony in support of LD 806 An Act to Amend the Scope of Practice for Expanded Function Dental Assistants.
Passage of LD 806 will allow Expanded Function Dental Assistants (EFDAs) to expose and process radiographs and further help to alleviate issues related to staffing shortages in dental practices across the state. They are well trained for this practice and requiring them to obtain a separate licensure for this is redundant and an unnecessary expense.
Thank you for your time and attention.
